prompt: In some areas, libraries, parks and community centres that were once run by paid council staff are now managed by local volunteers. Some people believe this is the best way to keep such services open, while others argue that local government should pay professionals to run them. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
essay:
As local authority budgets have tightened, many councils have handed libraries, parks and community centres to groups of residents who run them without pay. Supporters see this as the only realistic way to keep such places open, while critics argue that running them is a basic duty of local government. I believe volunteers can enrich these services but should not be expected to replace the people paid to provide them.

The case for volunteer management is stronger than it first appears. When the alternative is closure, a library open three days a week with volunteer staff is clearly preferable to a locked building. Residents who give their time also tend to develop a sense of ownership that a council department rarely inspires; they notice when a play area is damaged, and they organise events that reflect what their neighbours actually want. For retired people in particular, volunteering can provide a routine and a social role they might otherwise lack.

Nevertheless, there are good reasons to treat these services as a public responsibility. A librarian does far more than lend books: she helps people complete job applications, teaches basic computer skills and recognises when a regular visitor needs support from other agencies. Such work requires training and continuity, and a rota of volunteers, however committed, cannot guarantee either. Volunteers are also easier to find in comfortable neighbourhoods than in deprived ones. There is, too, a question of fairness, since residents are effectively being asked to donate labour for a service their taxes were supposed to fund.

In my view, the best arrangement is a small core of professional staff, supported by volunteers who extend opening hours and run additional activities. This retains the expertise and reliability that the public is entitled to while still drawing on the energy of the local people. Handing a service entirely to volunteers should be treated as an emergency measure, not as a model.
title: Volunteers running local services
